title: Happy Students
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n, determine the number of ways to select a group of students such that each student is either selected with more students chosen afterward or not selected with fewer students chosen afterward.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n, determine the number of ways to select a group of students such that each student is either selected with more students chosen afterward or not selected with fewer students chosen afterward.
constraints: nums has n entries from zero through n-1.
A selected student requires selected_count>nums[i]; an unselected student requires selected_count<nums[i].
Count selection groups for which every student is happy.
reference_solution:
def count_happy_student_groups(nums):
    values=sorted(nums);size=len(values);answer=0
    for selected in range(size+1):
        chosen_ok=selected==0 or values[selected-1]<selected
        unchosen_ok=selected==size or values[selected]>selected
        answer+=chosen_ok and unchosen_ok
    return answer

hints: For a fixed group size, the selected students must be exactly those with thresholds below that size.
Sort thresholds and test every cut between selected and unselected prefixes.
At cut s require values[s-1]<s when s>0 and values[s]>s when s<n.
These inequalities make precisely the first s sorted students eligible for selection and every remaining student eligible for omission, so each valid size defines one valid group.
